<a id="g-01"></a>
## G-01. Validation pipeline - how the gates map to BacktestLoop tools

The conceptual gates below remain the standard of correctness, but in BacktestLoop the agent executes them through the platform tools rather than local scripts:

| Gate | What it checks | BacktestLoop execution |
|---|---|---|
| V1 manifest completeness | Every ambiguity resolved or visibly defaulted | Decompose the rules and plan the implementation before writing code |
| V2 source/static checks | Syntax; no hallucinated APIs; no forbidden behavior | `check_python_syntax` on `strategy.py` + self-review against [G-03](#g-03) and the registries; a review of the code against the user's rules |
| V3-V5 capability/compile/indicator | Symbols exist; code imports; indicators produce sane values | The run itself is the gate - run the backtest (`run_backtest`); diagnose a failure via `get_backtest_status` and `get_backtest_log` |
| V6 signal diagnostics | Signal counts and timing are plausible | `print()` signal counts inside `signals()`/`next()`; read them in the execution output |
| V7 portfolio smoke | Simulation completes; results finite | `run_backtest` |
| V8 no-lookahead | No future information reaches signals | Code-level discipline ([G-08](#g-08)) - audit shifts, windows, HTF alignment during review |
| V9 sensitivity/edge cases | Plausible behavior across regimes | Experiments (`run_experiments`) for parameter/edge variations when warranted |
| V10 result validation | Result is plausible before presenting | Mandatory plausibility check: inspect equity/drawdown curves (`get_result`), trade counts, degenerate-result explanations |

A later gate must not run when an earlier gate fails for a clear reason: do not launch a full run when the syntax check fails, and do not present results while the execution log shows a runtime error. After a failed run, read the execution output, classify the error ([G-10](#g-10)), patch only the failing layer, and re-run (up to 3 retries).

<a id="g-02"></a>
## G-02. V1 - Manifest completeness

Reject or default visibly when any of these are unresolved:

- engine;
- data fields/timeframe/timezone;
- calculation profile;
- indicator period and convention;
- entry and exit conditions;
- signal timestamp and fill timestamp;
- long/short and pyramiding behavior;
- size rule;
- commission and slippage;
- stop/target units;
- initial cash;
- annualization frequency.

A missing exit rule is not automatically “hold forever.” A missing short rule is not automatically permission to short.

<a id="g-03"></a>
## G-03. V2 - Static checks (self-review checklist)

`check_python_syntax` catches only syntax. **A hallucinated API passes the syntax check and kills the paid run at runtime** - so before running, re-read the generated file against this list:

**Forbidden symbol references** (do not exist in the platform engines; every one has burned someone):

```text
Backtrader:  bt.ind.OBV   bt.ind.VWAP   bt.ind.SuperTrend   bt.ind.Fractal
VectorBT:    vbt.SMA  vbt.EMA  vbt.WMA  vbt.ROC  vbt.ADX  vbt.DMI  vbt.CCI
             vbt.MFI  vbt.CMF  vbt.VWAP  vbt.PSAR  vbt.Ichimoku
             vbt.SuperTrend  vbt.DonchianChannels
vbt-pro:     vbt.PF   wtype=...   sim_* arguments
```

The only native vbt factories are `MA, MSTD, BBANDS, RSI, STOCH, MACD, ATR, OBV`. Everything else: registry alias (Appendix A), pandas recipe (F-02), or canonical kernel (E-02).

**Hazard patterns to reject on sight:**

- positive line indices (`line[1]`) in Backtrader logic - future buffer access;
- `.shift(-1)`, centered rolling windows, full-sample normalization - lookahead;
- Python `and`/`or` on Backtrader line objects in `__init__`;
- a missing import for anything used (`pd.`, `np.` with no import - passes syntax, fails at runtime);
- network, subprocess, filesystem, `eval`/`exec`, or dynamic package installs inside strategy code - the strategy has no business doing any of these (the platform injects all data);
- engine wiring of any kind: `bt.Cerebro`, `bt.feeds.*`, `setcommission`, `vbt.Portfolio.*` in the `signals()` path;
- both `import backtrader` and `import vectorbt` in one file (breaks engine auto-detection).

<a id="g-04"></a>
## G-04. V3 - Capability preflight

The platform pins the engine versions, and the registries in this manual (Appendix A for Backtrader, Appendix B for VectorBT) were introspected against exactly those versions - **they are the preflight**. Resolve every indicator class, alias, parameter name, and output line through them before writing the strategy body; never from memory of another library or another vectorbt edition.

When something is genuinely uncertain (an optional integration, an enum member), embed a temporary introspection print in the strategy and read it from the run's output (`get_result_console_output` after a completed run, `get_backtest_log` after a failed one):

```python
import vectorbt as vbt
print("MA contract:", vbt.MA.input_names, vbt.MA.param_names, vbt.MA.output_names)
```

Remove diagnostic prints once resolved. Optional integrations must be verified this way before their outputs are referenced ([D-15](manual-d-vectorbt.md#d-15)).

<a id="g-05"></a>
## G-05. V4/V5 - Compile, import, and indicator sanity

In BacktestLoop there is no local fixture harness - **the run is the fixture**: it executes the strategy on the job's real data with the real engine versions. To make it informative, temporarily embed cheap indicator sanity prints in the strategy and read them from the execution output:

```python
# temporary diagnostics inside signals() - remove once verified
rsi_vals = rsi.dropna()
print(f"rsi: n={len(rsi_vals)}, min={rsi_vals.min():.1f}, max={rsi_vals.max():.1f}")
print(f"warm-up NaNs: {int(rsi.isna().sum())}")
```

What the sanity checks should establish:

- shape and alignment with the primary index;
- expected output names resolved (no `AttributeError`);
- warm-up count roughly matches the registry ([B-04](manual-b-data-math-timing.md#b-04));
- finite values after warm-up;
- bounded outputs (RSI in `[0,100]`; Bollinger upper ≥ middle ≥ lower; Supertrend direction in `{-1, 1}`).

A violated bound means the indicator implementation or its inputs are wrong - fix that layer; do not paper over it in signal logic.

<a id="g-06"></a>
## G-06. V6 - Signal diagnostics

Before simulation, record:

```python

def summarize_signal(name: str, signal: pd.Series | pd.DataFrame) -> dict[str, object]:
    values = signal.fillna(False).astype(bool)
    stacked = values.stack() if isinstance(values, pd.DataFrame) else values
    true_index = stacked[stacked].index
    return {
        "name": name,
        "shape": values.shape,
        "true_count": int(stacked.sum()),
        "first_true": None if len(true_index) == 0 else str(true_index[0]),
        "last_true": None if len(true_index) == 0 else str(true_index[-1]),
    }
```

Compare raw and shifted signals. If raw entries exist but shifted entries do not, the only true signal may have occurred on the final bar. If no raw signal exists, inspect indicator warm-up and rule thresholds rather than changing execution code.

Signal invariants:

- entries/exits are Boolean after NaN handling;
- no signal exists before all required indicators are ready;
- long and short conflicts match the explicit policy;
- a prior-bar breakout channel is non-NaN before a breakout is evaluated;
- event signals are not accidentally levels that remain true for weeks unless accumulation is intended.

<a id="g-07"></a>
## G-07. V7 - Portfolio smoke run

A strategy is executed with `run_backtest` (the full engine pipeline on the backtest's own window). After each run:

- read the execution output for errors, warnings (margin rejections, over-accumulation notices), and your diagnostic prints;
- check the result has a finite final value and a plausible trade count;
- inspect the equity/drawdown curves (`get_result`) - the curves are the only way to see whether growth is steady or one lucky spike.

Zero trades are not an exception by themselves - but they must be explained (warm-up longer than the window, thresholds never reached, signals misaligned), never presented as a mysterious success and never "fixed" by inventing trades. Compare the printed raw signal counts against the executed order count: signals present but no orders usually means every entry was rejected by the affordability check or the entries never coincided with a flat position.

<a id="g-08"></a>
## G-08. V8 - No-lookahead review

The agent cannot run perturbation harnesses before a job executes, so lookahead is prevented at **review time**. Before running, answer each of these for the generated code:

**Prefix-invariance question.** If all data after bar `t` were multiplied by 10, would any indicator or signal value at or before `t` change? It must not. Anything that fails this mentally is leakage: `.shift(-1)`, `rolling(..., center=True)`, full-sample normalization (`(x - x.mean()) / x.std()` over the whole series), min-max scaling over the full window, misaligned merges, or ML features fit on the full dataset. Normalize with *rolling/expanding* statistics only.

**Signal/fill question.** Under the platform conventions ([B-02](manual-b-data-math-timing.md#b-02)): in BOTH engines an order decided from bar `t` fills at open(t+1). Every input to the bar-`t` signal must be knowable by close(t).

**Breakout-channel question.** A channel meant to trigger on bar `t` must be built from bars before `t` - Donchian upper is `max(high[t-n:t])`, never a window containing `high[t]` (the rule becomes self-referential or impossible).

**Higher-timeframe availability question.** An HTF value may influence a lower-timeframe bar only from the first LTF bar *after* the HTF bar completed. In Backtrader this is the `len(htf)` gate ([C-12](manual-c-backtrader.md#c-12)); in vbt it is `reindex(...).ffill()` of a *completed-bar* series ([D-17](manual-d-vectorbt.md#d-17)) - never a backward merge of the day's final close into that day's earlier bars.

**ML question.** Train/fit windows must precede prediction windows; no leakage through scalers, encoders, or feature selection fit on the full sample.

If a live result looks too good (Sharpe ≫ 3, near-monotonic equity), treat lookahead as the prime suspect and re-run this review before presenting anything.

<a id="g-09"></a>
## G-09. V9 - Sensitivity and edge cases

When results matter (before recommending or tracking a strategy), probe robustness with the platform's experiments and date-range variations:

- parameter neighborhoods via `run_experiments` (a strategy that only works at `fast=10, slow=30` exactly is curve-fit);
- different market regimes via date ranges that include rising, falling, and flat stretches - and enough trades to mean something (a 3-trade sample proves nothing);
- warm-up sanity: a window barely longer than the longest indicator period should produce zero-to-few trades, not garbage values;
- sizing stress: margin-rejection warnings in the execution output mean the sizing rule outruns the account.

Expected properties:

- adding positive costs should not improve final value solely through accounting;
- RSI should remain bounded;
- ATR should be nonnegative;
- Supertrend direction should be `-1` or `1` after warm-up;
- orders should not precede signals;
- a flat series should not produce infinite position sizes;
- a zero volatility risk denominator should prevent entry rather than divide by zero.

<a id="g-10"></a>
## G-10. Error taxonomy and targeted repair

| Error code | Layer | Example | Repair action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ENV_PACKAGE_MISSING` | Environment | `ModuleNotFoundError: talib` | Use a package from the standard environment (the packages rule in SKILL.md); a `requirements.txt` works only where the server allows extra packages; TA-Lib cannot be installed → use the documented custom route |
| `ENV_VERSION_MISMATCH` | Environment | package requires newer pandas/Numba | Platform-pinned; pick an implementation that works on the shipped versions - do not rewrite strategy semantics |
| `API_SYMBOL_MISSING` | Capability | `vbt.ADX` missing | Resolve support registry/integration/custom implementation |
| `API_OUTPUT_MISMATCH` | Capability | `.upperband` missing | Inspect exact output names |
| `DATA_SCHEMA_INVALID` | Data | missing `volume`, duplicate dates | Normalize/reject data |
| `DATA_ALIGNMENT_INVALID` | Data | signal columns differ from close | Explicitly align index/columns |
| `INDICATOR_WARMUP` | Indicator | all NaN on short dataset | Extend data or reduce documented period; never fill zero silently |
| `INDICATOR_CONVENTION` | Indicator | RSI differs across engines | Apply selected profile |
| `NUMBA_TYPING` | Implementation | pandas object in `@njit` or object-typed signals | Convert outside callback; pass arrays/scalars; cast signals to Boolean |
| `NUMBA_CACHE_LOCATOR` | Runtime packaging | `no locator available` for `cache=True` | Use plain `@njit` (no `cache=True`) in strategy files - the sandbox has no stable file locator |
| `SIGNAL_NO_EVENTS` | Strategy | no crosses | Diagnose rules/data; do not fabricate orders |
| `SIGNAL_CONFLICT` | Strategy | long and short same bar | Apply explicit conflict policy |
| `LOOKAHEAD_DETECTED` | Timing | future perturbation changes past | Fix shifts/windows/resampling |
| `ORDER_REJECTED` | Broker | margin/cash/size | Inspect order status and sizing |
| `STOP_AMBIGUITY` | Simulation | stop and target inside one OHLC bar | State assumption or use finer data |
| `RESOURCE_LIMIT` | Runtime | huge grid/compilation | Reduce grid, cache, batch, or enforce quotas |

Repair sequence:

```text
classify error -> preserve manifest -> patch one layer -> rerun failed gate ->
rerun all later gates -> compare semantics -> return validation report
```

Do not make several unrelated changes in one repair. A valid fix should explain the failed invariant.

<a id="g-11"></a>
## G-11. Final acceptance checklist

A strategy is acceptable only when all applicable items are true:

- [ ] Engine chosen per [A-04](manual-a-operating-contract.md#a-04) (VectorBT default; Backtrader only for genuinely event-driven logic) and auto-detection markers present, never mixed.
- [ ] Correct authoring shape: `def signals(data, params)` (or `build_portfolio`) / `class Strategy(bt.Strategy)` named exactly `Strategy`.
- [ ] Backtrader only: `live_resume_replay_safe = True` declared in the class body (or the `live_resume_state()`/`load_live_resume_state(state)` hooks for genuinely path-dependent state) - live paper deploys refuse the strategy without it. VectorBT strategies need nothing (inherently replay-safe).
- [ ] All imports present (`vbt`/`pd`/`np`/`bt` as used) - including inside experiment file overrides.
- [ ] No platform-owned code: no data loading/feeds, no Cerebro, no `setcommission`/fees, no `vbt.Portfolio.*` in the signals path, no hardcoded symbols/timeframes/dates/paths.
- [ ] All indicator classes/functions resolved through the registry or approved custom code; exact output names verified; no vbt-pro APIs.
- [ ] Calculation profile chosen and conventions consistent.
- [ ] Warm-up preserved as NaN/no-trade; boolean signals end `.fillna(False).astype(bool)` where NaN is possible.
- [ ] Signal/fill timing consistent with [B-02](manual-b-data-math-timing.md#b-02); no lookahead per the [G-08](#g-08) review.
- [ ] No current-bar breakout self-reference.
- [ ] Position/order guards prevent duplicate entries (Backtrader); level-vs-pulse signal shape chosen deliberately (vbt - entries are edge-triggered by the runner).
- [ ] Long/short and reversal behavior explicit; shorts via negative size in the vbt signals path.
- [ ] Sizing explicit and IMPLEMENTED, matching the plan (vbt: a bare 2-tuple is 1-unit sizing - include the [D-05](manual-d-vectorbt.md#d-05) size series unless single-unit trades were requested; account size read from `params`, never assumed to auto-contain `initial_cash`). Default percent-of-equity stated in one line when assumed.
- [ ] Stops use documented units and intrabar assumptions.
- [ ] Syntax check passed; strategy reviewed against the user's rules; the run completed and its output read.
- [ ] Equity/drawdown curves inspected; result plausibility-checked; zero-trade or degenerate results explained, never dressed up.
